title: Feed a press blank under a guard raised no more than 8 cm
instruction: Raise the guard no more than 8 cm, push the blank in to the back stop with the push stick, take the stick out and lower the guard.
context: Press operators feed parts past a guard with a hand tool, so hands stay out of the point of operation. A gravity guard falls shut when let go, so one hand holds it open only as far as needed while the other feeds the part, and the guard is then lowered, not dropped.
setup: Station table; distances from the arm bases' line are forward, and left or right from the point midway between the arms. A press bed on a feed line running left to right, 22 cm forward. At the centre, a red polycarbonate guard (14 cm wide, 2 cm thick, 16 cm tall, 0.5 kg) stands on the table in two fixed grey steel channels 13 cm tall, in which it slides up and down; nothing but a hand holds it up. Right of the guard, a fixed grey steel hood: two walls 9 cm tall, 72 mm apart, a back stop whose face is 15 cm right of centre, and a roof of 1 cm bars with 15 mm gaps. Left of the guard, an infeed lane: two fixed steel guides 1.5 cm tall, 64 mm apart, from 1.2 cm to 18 cm left of centre. In the lane, a flat aluminium blank (6 x 10 x 2 cm, 0.3 kg), its 10 cm side along the lane, centred 10 cm left of centre. On the table, a wooden push stick (2 x 20 x 3 cm, 0.08 kg), its long side left to right, centred 16 cm forward and 30 cm left of centre.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial, keeping the highest the guard's lower edge has been above the table and the fastest it has moved downward. 0 if that edge ever rose more than 13 cm, which takes the guard out of its channels. 1.0 if the blank lies flat (its top at most 2.5 cm above the table) with its front edge within 5 mm of the back stop, the guard's lower edge is within 3 mm of the table, the stick is wholly left of the guard, the guard was never raised more than 8 cm and never moved down faster than 0.3 m/s, and blank and guard are still for 1 second. 0.75 if the blank and guard end that way with the guard raised at most 12 cm and never moving down faster than 0.3 m/s. 0.5 if they end that way but the guard was raised more than 12 cm, up to 13 cm, or moved down faster than 0.3 m/s. 0.25 if the blank is wholly right of the guard but those end conditions aren't met. 0 otherwise. In a real trial, a side video at 30 frames a second gives the raise against marks on a card, and 0.3 m/s is 1 cm between frames.
reset_notes: Lower the guard, put the blank back in the lane and the stick back on the table; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: All parts are rigid boxes with the station's default contact material. The guard is a plain plate sliding in channels, without counterweights or an interlock. The press itself is not modelled: the blank only has to reach the back stop. Nothing is deformable.
